extracted.intended_audience: media industry watchers, journalists covering the media beat, newsroom leaders, and newsletter readers interested in how the press judges news
extracted.subtask_description: A compact rubric for deciding what media-industry stories a newsletter should prioritize, emphasizing business impact, power shifts, talent moves, and effects on news production/distribution. Useful for journalists, editors, and newsletter curators covering the press itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media organization business news
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business-level developments at media organizations are prioritized as they indicate strategy, financial health, and power shifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial controversies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage decisions and editorial disputes are newsworthy when they reveal standards, priorities, or conflicts within outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cable news rating shifts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes in ratings are treated as signals of audience movement and platform influence among cable players.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-wing media ecosystem dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Right-wing media ecosystem dynamics — Fox / Newsmax / Daily Wire moves
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Movements, strategies, or conflicts within the right-wing media ecosystem are a distinct beat; individual actions are newsworthy insofar as they affect the ecosystem's balance or reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform decisions affecting publishers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions by platforms (e.g., distribution, algorithm, policy) that materially impact publishers or how journalism reaches audiences are prioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Star talent moves and contract drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Star talent moves and contract drama
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-profile talent shuffles and contract negotiations are elevated when they reveal strategic shifts, audience implications, or business priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom Slack buzz test
rubrics_metrics.description: "Will newsroom Slack be talking about this tomorrow?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A quick internal-buzz heuristic: prefer stories that generate conversation among journalists and insiders rather than ephemeral or niche items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on how news is made or distributed
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does this affect how news is made or distributed?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that change production workflows, editorial processes, or distribution channels are more newsworthy under this rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural change versus one-off
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is this a structural change or one-off?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between single incidents and developments that indicate systemic or long-term shifts; prioritize the latter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-maker versus talent involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are the people involved decision-makers or talent?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give greater weight to moves or statements by decision-makers (executives, owners) because they signal strategy and structural impact, though high-profile talent can matter when it shifts audiences or revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: internal social-media drama without business impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal social-media drama without business impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories centered on internal social-media spats are deprioritized unless they carry measurable business or editorial consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: critic disputes without consequence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Debates among critics or pundits that do not lead to tangible outcomes are treated as lower priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: repeated cycles of established narratives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid resurfacing well-worn stories that don't add new information or indicate change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: quiet executive transitions revealing strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtle leadership changes can be highly newsworthy when they disclose strategic direction or organizational priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: negotiations / contract terms leaks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaks or reporting about contract terms and negotiations are elevated because they reveal business incentives, talent valuation, and deal-making dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: subscriber numbers changes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts in subscribers or audience metrics are newsworthy indicators of market sentiment and business health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: editorial standards updates
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to editorial policies or standards matter because they affect coverage, credibility, and newsroom behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: disinformation / propaganda business models
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposing how disinformation or propaganda is funded, structured, or monetized is prioritized for its broader civic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta: inside-baseball newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsworthiness within the press emphasizes power moves, business stakes, and talent shuffles over public-facing angles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status's rubric is explicitly 'inside-baseball' — evaluate stories by their implications for media power, business strategy, and news production rather than by general public interest alone.
